subtitle: Spain and France lead the 2026 World Cup winner market at similar implied probabilities around 16-17 percent, with England close behind, reflecting their status as the top European sides entering the expanded 48-team tournament. Spain’s edge stems from recent European Championship success under Luis de la Fuente and standout performers like Lamine Yamal, while France maintains elite depth featuring Kylian Mbappé and strong recent results. England’s consistent path to major finals and solid qualifying form keep them competitive. The bunched pricing captures the parity among these squads, all boasting high-quality attacking options and defensive organization, alongside the inherent unpredictability of a summer tournament in North America where any of several contenders could advance deep based on form, injuries, or key matches.
